# `prefer-typed-io-parameter`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports an `anytype` writer or reader parameter that is only the receiver of
`std.Io.Writer` or `std.Io.Reader` method calls.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Since Zig 0.15, `std.Io.Writer` and `std.Io.Reader` are concrete interfaces
rather than generic types, so a function that only writes or reads through one
can take `*std.Io.Writer` or `*std.Io.Reader`. The typed parameter documents
what the function needs, compiles one copy instead of one per caller's stream
type, and reports a misuse at the call site instead of inside the body. It is
also the signature `{f}` formatting expects of a `format` method.

## When it fires

It fires on an `anytype` parameter named like a stream (containing `writer` or
`reader`, or `w`, `out`, `r`, `input` and similar) when every reference to it in
the function is the receiver of a method call, each method exists on the 0.17
interface with the same number of arguments, and there is at least one such
call. A parameter that is passed to another function, reflected on with
`@TypeOf`, accessed as a field, or called with a method from the pre-0.15
generic API (`writeByteNTimes`, `readByte`, one-argument `writeStruct`) stays
`anytype`, as does the parameter of a `jsonStringify` method, which `std.json`
calls with its `*std.json.Stringify`. There is no automatic fix: the callers
must pass the interface.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const Point = struct {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,

    pub fn format(point: Point, writer: anytype) !void {
        try writer.print("({d}, {d})", .{ point.x, point.y });
    }
};
```
